high_level_description: Strictly non-photographic, wordless early Andean ink-and-flat-color manuscript illustration: an Inka khipukamayuq adds contribution cords to one public khipu after two equal-sized workers deliver completed woven panels; many panels create only a moderately denser knot group, older cords remain attached in muted earth colors, and no money, throne or ranking appears.

compositional_deconstruction.background: A pale fiber-paper field is enclosed by a thin dark-brown stepped border and divided into one continuous frontal gathering space by a single ochre ground band. Sparse flat mountain contours occupy only the upper corners. The drawing uses dark ink outlines, red earth, ochre, indigo and muted brown without realistic depth, photographic light, gradient, alphabet, numeral, caption, arrow, chart, coin, crown, throne, leaderboard, state emblem or modern device.

elements.desc: Large public khipu suspended horizontally across the center from a plain wooden beam, with one thick ochre primary cord and distinct red, indigo, cream and brown pendant cords attached in an unbroken sequence. Recent pendants have crisp knot clusters, older brown pendants remain fully attached but visually muted; no cord is labeled, cut, crowned, monetized or raised above the others.

Adult Inka khipukamayuq seated at the lower-right, medium-brown skin, straight black shoulder-length hair, plain indigo tunic, red-earth mantle and simple sandals. With a focused neutral expression, both hands attach a new pendant to the existing primary cord while preserving every earlier cord; they hold no scepter, coin, crown, weapon, ballot, written ledger or universal authority symbol.

Adult Andean worker standing at the lower-left, dark-brown skin, long black hair tied back, ochre tunic, cream mantle and simple sandals. They present one completed red-and-indigo woven panel with both hands at chest height, standing at the same scale as the other worker and carrying no money pouch, badge, medal, title, voting token, oversized hardware or submissive posture.

Second adult Andean worker standing near the center, medium-brown skin, straight black hair at shoulder length, red-earth tunic, indigo mantle and simple sandals. They present a thick bundled stack of completed cream-and-indigo woven panels, yet remain the same physical size and height as the first worker; no wealth display, crown, platform, rank badge, coin or command gesture appears.

Single completed woven panel offered by the first worker, rectangular and flat with alternating red-earth, indigo and cream stepped bands. A short new pendant beside it carries a small clear knot group, recording the accepted contribution without consuming the panel; neither object bears letters, numerals, signature, price, ownership seal, award ribbon or sacred emblem.

Bundled stack of completed woven panels offered by the second worker, tied loosely with a plain cream cord so several layers remain visible. Its corresponding new indigo pendant carries a denser but only moderately larger knot group than the first worker's red pendant, expressing compressed returns without a giant branch, coin pile, trophy, rank pedestal or numerical score.
